t: The Aghlabid conquest of Sicily began with a landing at Mazara del Vallo in 827 and took Palermo in 831, but the island was not fully conquered until Taormina fell in 902.
From 948 the Kalbid dynasty ruled Sicily as autonomous emirs while formally acknowledging the Fatimid caliphs.
Arab rule brought land reforms, qanat irrigation and new crops such as oranges, lemons, pistachio and sugarcane.
dyk: Ibn Hawqal, a Baghdad merchant who visited Palermo in 950, reckoned 7,000 butchers trading in 150 shops in the city.
ev: Aghlabid forces under Asad ibn al-Furat land at Mazara del Vallo and win the first battle on 15 July
Palermo falls in September after a year-long siege and becomes the Muslim capital of Sicily
The conquest of the island is completed with the fall of Taormina
The Fatimid caliph al-Mansur appoints al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kalbi governor, the first emir of the Kalbid dynasty
A Christian army under Emperor Otto II is defeated at Stilo, but Emir Abu'l-Qasim is killed in the battle
Under al-Hasan al-Samsam the island breaks into four qadits
Butera, Noto and Malta, the last Arab strongholds, fall to the Normans

f.founder: The Aghlabid dynasty of Ifriqiya, whose conquest was led by the qadi Asad ibn al-Furat; al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kalbi was the first Kalbid emir
